source_name: Ministry of MSME & KVIC, Government of India

sections.heading: Scheme Overview and Objectives
sections.content: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a flagship credit-linked subsidy programme launched by the Ministry of MSME. It aims to generate continuous, sustainable employment opportunities in rural and urban areas by helping micro-entrepreneurs set up new self-employment ventures and micro-enterprises in manufacturing and service sectors.

sections.heading: Maximum Project Cost and Financial Assistance
sections.content: The maximum permissible project cost for setting up a new unit in the Manufacturing Sector is Rs. 50 Lakhs. The maximum permissible project cost for setting up a new unit in the Business/Service Sector is Rs. 20 Lakhs. For upgradation of existing well-performing PMEGP/MUDRA units, a second loan of up to Rs. 1 Crore for manufacturing and Rs. 25 Lakhs for service is available with a 15% to 20% subsidy.

sections.heading: Margin Money Subsidy Rates
sections.content:
In Rural Areas: General Category beneficiaries receive a 25% Government Subsidy (Margin Money), requiring only 10% own contribution. Special Categories (including SC, ST, OBC, Women, Minorities, Ex-servicemen, Differently-abled, and Transgenders) receive a 35% Government Subsidy in rural areas with only 5% own contribution.
In Urban Areas: General Category receives 15% subsidy (10% own contribution), while Special Categories receive 25% subsidy (5% own contribution).

sections.heading: Eligibility and Educational Criteria
sections.content: Any individual above 18 years of age is eligible. For setting up manufacturing units with project cost above Rs. 10 Lakhs and service units above Rs. 5 Lakhs, the applicant must have passed at least standard 8th examination. Self Help Groups (SHGs), Charitable Trusts, and Co-operative Societies are also eligible. Existing units or units that have already availed government subsidies are not eligible.

sections.heading: Bank Loan and Repayment Schedule
sections.content: Banks provide the balance 90% to 95% of the total project cost as a composite loan (term loan for plant/machinery and working capital). The repayment schedule ranges from 3 to 7 years after an initial moratorium period determined by the financing bank.
